# Risk register — Gosling shared shell productization

Status vocabulary: `open`, `mitigating`, `closed`, `accepted`. Review at every gate exit.

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Prevention / mitigation | Trigger / contingency | Owner / gate | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SHP-RSK-001 | Reusing full Desktop `main.ts`/preload gives shells broad filesystem/settings/provider authority and defeats minimal-host intent | high | critical | Separate shell entry/preload; typed IPC allowlist; no branch inside full Desktop renderer; negative-space tests | Any shell imports full preload/main IPC registry → stop Gate 4 and extract boundary | Runtime, G2–5 | open |
| SHP-RSK-002 | Electron app identity is set after userData/single-instance/protocol initialization, causing cross-product collisions | medium | critical | Resolve profile and set app identity before readiness/lock; app identity unit and coexistence tests | Shared path/lock/protocol observed → block Gate 6 and repair ordering | Runtime, G3–6 | open |
| SHP-RSK-003 | Forge/workflow/platform scripts derive different names/IDs/assets from independent environment values | high | high | Canonical profile resolution/hash; thin adapters; package readback; collision checks | Any artifact field differs from manifest → artifact invalid, no upload | Build, G3/7 | open |
| SHP-RSK-004 | Product profile becomes a second runtime/config/credential authority | medium | critical | Strict profile/provisioning split; no secret/settings/provider values; Rust remains validation authority | Requested profile field encodes runtime secret/policy semantics → plan review, likely reject | Architecture, G2–4 | open |
| SHP-RSK-005 | Renderer can assert shell identity/namespace/provisioning through IPC/ACP parameters | low | critical | No such preload operations; compare runtime metadata to fixed profile; server-fixed existing contract | Mismatch or renderer parameter surface → fail closed and regression test | Security, G4/6 | open |
| SHP-RSK-006 | Unit/source tests pass while packaged binary/resource/CSP/preload path fails | high | high | Actual packaged E2E, resource verifier, tamper tests, launch/restart/cleanup evidence | Packaged test unavailable on target → cannot mark target release-ready | QA, G6–8 | open |
| SHP-RSK-007 | Child process leaks or stale process-registry entry survives startup/crash/quit | medium | high | One lifecycle owner; bounded graceful/forced cleanup; PID/registry tests and installed replay | Any orphan after test → gate blocker; retain diagnostics and patch root cause | Runtime, G4/6 | open |
| SHP-RSK-008 | Diagnostics expose server secrets, credential values, prompts, paths, or unbounded logs | medium | critical | Allowlisted fields, sentinel redaction, byte ceilings, private atomic write, inspect-before-share warning | Sentinel appears or bundle too broad → block release; rotate any exposed test secret | Security, G4–8 | open |
| SHP-RSK-009 | Handoff silently widens authority or accepts forged destination/reference data | medium | critical | Server-prepared versioned envelope; explicit confirmation; protocol allowlist; no renderer-built envelope | Invalid destination/version/ref or no confirmation → deny and diagnose | Security, G4–6 | open |
| SHP-RSK-010 | Existing V8 helper/version/checksum mismatch leads to bypassing archive verification | low | critical | Wrapper/build-script contract confirmed; retain immutable checksums and fail closed; add cold/warm/corrupt/unsupported tests | Missing checksum/asset → operator seed/build-from-source; never disable check | CI/supply chain, G0–1 | mitigating |

| SHP-RSK-015 | Fixture is mistaken for a real product or accidentally becomes publishable/updateable | medium | high | Explicit fixture IDs/version/banner/assets; immutable `publishable:false`; workflow deny; no production feed | Fixture reaches release/upload/sign path → incident/block, delete draft artifact | Test/release, G3–7 | open |
| SHP-RSK-016 | Compatibility metadata is incomplete, so a newer shell/core pair proceeds and corrupts or misreads state | medium | high | Exact bundled-core policy; compare profile/build/runtime/schema/method metadata before session; rollback tests | Unknown/mismatch → fail closed before session/migration | Runtime, G2/4/6 | open |
| SHP-RSK-017 | Compatibility checks duplicate/generated DTOs drift from canonical Rust ACP contract | medium | high | Use generated SDK/types; additive Rust metadata only when required; schema regeneration/check | Hand-authored duplicate shell DTO found → remove and regenerate | Architecture, G2/4 | open |
| SHP-RSK-018 | Broad edits to 3,399-line `main.ts` create unrelated Desktop regressions | high | high | New shell entry/modules; router-only bounded edits; review diff and full Desktop suite | Domain/lifecycle rules added to `main.ts` → stop and extract | Architecture, G3–5 | open |
| SHP-RSK-019 | Release workflow duplication creates four drifting platform implementations | high | high | Shared resolver/action and reusable adapters; platform-specific code only where necessary | Same rule implemented differently in multiple workflows → consolidate before Gate 7 exit | Release, G7 | open |
| SHP-RSK-020 | Signing/notarization/updater testing needs credentials or predecessor artifact unavailable to agent | high | medium | Separate human gate; unsigned structural/smoke proof; explicit unverified status | Missing credential/predecessor → do not claim release-ready/published/updater-ready | Maintainer, G7–8 | open |
| SHP-RSK-021 | Package tests become flaky due to polling, process timing, or OS services | medium | high | Observable readiness/events, deterministic temp roots, PID diagnostics; no retry-only fix | Repeated pass-after-retry → defect and root-cause work, not green evidence | QA, G4/6 | open |
| SHP-RSK-022 | Shared configuration is accidentally isolated, breaking intentional credential/profile reuse, or runtime state is accidentally shared | medium | high | Explicit path matrix; app identity tests; backend `RuntimePaths` assertions; coexistence sentinel tests | Approved shared/isolated path differs → block Gate 6 and correct path owner | Runtime/data, G3/6 | open |
| SHP-RSK-023 | Deep links or external navigation open arbitrary schemes/hosts or cross product boundary | medium | critical | Profile-specific scheme; strict URL parse/action allowlist; target ownership tests; full Gosling handoff allowlist | Unknown action/scheme/host → ignore/diagnose, never forward | Security, G4/6 | open |
| SHP-RSK-024 | Product-specific icons/assets are missing or wrong but build silently falls back to Gosling assets | high | medium | Required asset matrix; no fallback for publishable shell; embedded/readback checks | Missing asset → profile check fails before Forge | Packaging, G3/7 | open |
| SHP-RSK-025 | New dependency expands supply chain or cannot run in Electron/CI targets | low | medium | Prefer existing stack/stdlib; dependency rationale/license/vulnerability/replacement cost | New dependency proposed → ADR note and all-target validation required | Architecture, G2/8 | open |
| SHP-RSK-026 | Domain requirements leak into shared fixture and overfit the host | medium | high | Neutral fixture, domain slot interface, negative-space audit, two fixture identities | Domain nouns/actions/payload interpretation appear → remove or require separate domain plan | Scope, all | open |
| SHP-RSK-027 | Scope expands into publishing real shells or updater promotion without explicit approval | low | critical | Plan-only authority; fixture non-publishability; human approvals retained | Any upload/sign/publish/update request absent explicit authorization → stop | Governance, G7–8 | open |
| SHP-RSK-028 | Current main changes significantly before implementation, invalidating paths/contracts | medium | medium | Gate 0 reorientation; dedicated worktree; plan-change record; reuse newer extractions | Baseline differs materially → amend file plan/sequence before edits | Execution, G0 | open |
| SHP-RSK-029 | Test ledgers/docs conventions evolve and new tests become untracked | medium | medium | Gate 0 inspect current conventions; update any active test inventory/ledger required by repo | New ledger appears or AGENTS changes → comply before test commit | Governance, all | open |
| SHP-RSK-030 | Signing/update/release identity differs between artifact metadata and OS registration | medium | critical | Post-package and installed readback per OS; updater remains disabled until verified | Any mismatch → reject artifact; do not patch metadata post-signing | Release, G7–8 | open |

## Risk acceptance rules

- Critical/high risks involving authority, secrets, process leaks, state collision, artifact cross-publication, workflow injection, unverified downloads, or incompatible state cannot be accepted for a public release.
- A platform/signing risk may remain open only when that target is explicitly not declared release-ready and the handoff names the missing human evidence.
- Every closed risk links to a regression test and final-revision evidence in the traceability matrix or defect ledger.
